explicitDate.note: The date must sit immediately after the trigger word (modulo 'on'/'by'). If the captured date fails to parse, evaluation falls through to withinDays.
explicitDate.reasonTemplate: Entry states a due date of {date}.

withinDays.reasonTemplate: Order or entry states an obligation within {days} days.

docTypeRules.note: No \b after 'complaint': 'first amended complaints' still matches.
Ordered before opposition/reply: 'Opposition to Defendant's MTD' is still a motion_to_dismiss.

factActorRules.note: Reachable only when no defendant/respondent/opposing word is present (e.g. bare 'MOTION to Dismiss the FAC').

filerRules.note: The 'ag ' alternative keeps its trailing space (matches 'AG reply' but not "AG's"); the group's closing \b applies after it.
No closing \b on the group: 'reassigned' matches via the 'reassign' prefix.
The /i flag is redundant (input is already lowercased) but kept for fidelity to the source literal.

note: Family 3 extraction: interpretation strategy moved out of code (strategy as data). The scripts under internal/scripts/courtlistener/ and internal/scripts/split-matter.mjs are dumb renderers over these rules. Ordered rule lists are first-match-wins; a rule with "pattern": null is the default. Regexes are strings compiled at load with the given flags. 'input' says whether the value is lowercased before testing ('lowercase') or tested raw ('raw'). Do not change values here without updating the golden fixtures in internal/src/data/courtlistener/fixtures/docket-interpretation.json.
